title: Session TTL lease reconciliation and burst crediting for intermittent clients
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Clients with flaky connectivity and mobile clients frequently reconnect mid-stream. Our current session leasing and TTL logic occasionally double-credits 'burst' token allowances when a reconnect happens within the TTL window, or conversely fails to return provisional credits when sessions are prematurely abandoned. This leads to inconsistent per-customer token tallies and incorrect quota enforcement in multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

Scope: Investigate the session lease lifecycle across the gateway, session service, and metering ledger. Implement deterministic reconciliation steps to ensure: 1) provisional burst credits granted to a session are idempotent across reconnects, 2) leases expired due to inactivity are reclaimed exactly once, 3) race conditions between gateway reconnect and ledger finalization do not cause orphaned credits. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and a staged rollout with metric-driven guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: No increase in 'ghost credits' for reconnecting sessions in the staging load test (target < 0.01% of sessions)
End-to-end unit and integration tests that simulate duplicate connect/resume, long reconnects, and split-brain gateway failovers
Metering ledger shows reversible provisional credits when sessions abort before final tokenization, with audit logs linking decisions to session lease IDs
Performance: added reconciliation logic must not increase median request tail latency by >1ms in the gateway path
Runbook updated and a canary rollout plan defined with abort criteria tied to billing delta and error rates
plan: Design: define canonical session lease model and idempotency token for provisional credits (design doc linked)
Implement gateway changes to attach lease-id and connection-attempt sequence number to session start/resume calls
Modify session-service to maintain a short-term lease table with deterministic reclaim semantics and a reconciliation endpoint
Update metering pipeline to accept provisional credits tagged with lease-id and to only finalize credits once a terminal event is observed or lease expires
Add comprehensive unit tests and a fault-injection integration test harness that covers reconnects, delayed finalization, and ledger races
Rollout: deploy session-service + gateway changes to canary region, monitor billing deltas and session metrics, then global rollout if stable
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after incident where customer reported unexpected token debits on intermittent mobile sessions. Initial investigation shows provisional credit duplication on reconnect.

2026-03-01 Marco Reyes: Spike completed. Prototype lease-id header appended by gateway; observed duplicate provisional credits in prototyping when resume requests race with ledger finalization. Suspect missing idempotency check in metering ingestion.
2026-03-04 Design note: Decided to use a 15s short TTL for provisional leases and an always-on reconciliation job that marks leases as 'finalizable' after a 2x TTL delay to avoid reclaim races.

2026-03-07 QA: Added integration scenarios for 'fast reconnect' (<=2s), 'slow reconnect' (10-30s), and 'orphan session' (>TTL). Found a race where gateway retries with stale sequence numbers; added sequence monotonicity guard.
2026-03-10 Marco Reyes: Implemented idempotency in metering ingestion. Added ledger tombstone records for reclaimed leases to prevent double-finalization. Preparing PR for review.

2026-03-10 Review notes: PM requested metrics for percent of sessions using provisional credits and the delta between provisional vs finalized billed tokens. Also requested a safe rollback plan that disables provisional credits gateway feature flag.
Next steps: finish PR, add canary monitors, and schedule the canary rollout window. Coordinate with Billing on audit queries to validate early canary data.
